Commentary.Commentary: We are back for India's reply. Jos Buttler and Co. head out to the centre. Rohit Sharma walks out to open the innings alongside the debutant Yashasvi Jaiswal. Jofra Archer will start with the new ball for the visitors. Two slips in place. Archer to Jaiswal first up. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, India will be the happier of the two sides at the halfway mark. The English openers found it easy to hit through the line against the new ball, but whether it moves around under lights remains to be seen. Similarly, Harshit Rana pointed out that the wicket is a bit two-paced, so it will be interesting to see if batting gets easier under the lights. Plenty to watch out for in the chase. India's chase coming up shortly!

Harshit Rana is up for a quick chat. He says he has worked hard for this debut and he is living his dream life. Adds that he is feeling great. Mentions that he was looking to bowl at a certain length and got rewarded for it. Tells that the English batters were looking to make room so he talked to Rohit Sharma and looked to keep it on the stumps from there on. Further mentions that it is a double-paced wicket and the odd ball keeps low and some kick off. Adds that the bowlers started well then bounced back later on. Says that it is a good total and they are confident in chasing it down.

Jos could not build on his half-century while Jacob Bethell looked scratchy at the start but grew in confidence as his innings progressed. He too fell immediately after scoring his fifty, and the tail was left exposed. Jofra Archer struck a few lusty blows, but eventually, England were bowled out for 248 with 14 balls left unused. For India, Harshit Rana was taken to the cleaners early on by Salt but he roared back with a double strike and finished with three wickets on his debut. In the spin department, Ravindra Jadeja was miserly as always with figures of 3 for 26 from 9 overs, including a maiden.

After opting to bat, Phil Salt went on the offensive against the debutant, Harshit Rana, and got England off to a flyer. A mix-up led to Salt's downfall as the tourists slipped from 75/0 to 77/3 in 8 balls. The English skipper Jos Buttler led the rebuild for his side and knew what the situation demanded of him. Root fell after a start, but Jos continued on his merry way by knocking the spinners around in the middle phase.

A job well done by India! While there’s plenty of joy in the Indian camp, England will be left disappointed, especially after their blistering start, racing to 71/0 in just 8 overs. A recurring pattern of the innings was that whenever England began to build a partnership, India struck to halt their momentum, often following up with another wicket to keep the visitors in check.

Commentary.Commentary: With the pre-match formalities complete, all eyes now turn to the action ahead! The two umpires make their way to the middle, followed closely by the Indian team, who charge into their positions. Striding out confidently for England are openers Phil Salt and Ben Duckett, ready to take on the challenge again. Mohammed Shami stands poised at the top of his mark, raring to go. Let's play says the umpire and here we go!
The match officials step onto the field, accompanied by both captains, as the teams line up with pride for the national anthems. It will be England's national anthem first followed by that of India.

The Indian skipper, Rohit Sharma says that they were anyway looking to bowl first. Shares that it is about understanding that it’s not just about what you want to do, but how you execute it. Mentions that the focus is on being aggressive with the ball and adjusting based on what unfolds thereafter. Tells that they had a good break, allowing them some time to reflect. Mentions that this series presents an opportunity to get back into the groove and do what's required. Adds that game time is crucial, especially since they’ve hardly played this format since the World Cup. Informs that Yashasvi Jaiswal and Harshit Rana will be making their debuts and Virat Kohli misses out because he had a right knee injury last night.

Jos Buttler, the skipper of England says that the group is nice and tight and with Joe Root back, it feels like will be a good game. Adds that the morale is high and they as a team have had their moments but will now aim to play well for longer periods. Mentions it's going to be a great test leading to the Champions Trophy and they are going in with 3 seamers and an extra spinning all-rounder.
England (Playing XI) - Ben Duckett, Phil Salt (WK), Joe Root, Harry Brook, Jos Buttler (C), Liam Livingstone, Jacob Bethell, Brydon Carse, Jofra Archer, Adil Rashid, Saqib Mahmood.

India (Playing XI) - Rohit Sharma (C), Yashasvi Jaiswal (On ODI debut), Shreyas Iyer, Shubman Gill, Hardik Pandya, Axar Patel, KL Rahul (WK), Ravindra Jadeja, Harshit Rana (On ODI debut), Kuldeep Yadav, Mohammed Shami.
TOSS - England win the toss and they will BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Deep Dasgupta is near the deck. He says that traditionally, it's not a high-scoring venue. Shares that the square boundaries measure 68 and 69 metres with the straight hit being 75 metres. Graeme Swann joins him and he says that the pitch is made up of red soil, with a few cracks here and there. Adds that it's a hard deck, with a tiny bit of grass, but not much moisture. Feels that spin could come into play later, especially given the nature of the red soil. Swann says that overall, it's shaping up to be a good cricket pitch for both teams.

JUST IN - Yashasvi Jaiswal and Harshit Rana have been presented with their maiden ODI caps in the Indian huddle. Jaiswal received his cap from captain Rohit Sharma, while Rana was handed his by Mohammed Shami.

As for England, the T20I series didn’t go their way, and their frailties against spin were evident. Joe Root, who will be playing his first ODI since the 2023 World Cup, is undoubtedly the best player against spin in the English setup, and his presence offers a much-needed boost. The tourists have already announced their playing XI, which features a three-pronged pace attack alongside a frontline spinner in Adil Rashid. How the batters fare against the Indian spinners will go a long way in deciding their fortunes in this series. Stick around for the toss and team news!

Since that ODI World Cup final defeat against Australia, India haven’t played much 50-over cricket, featuring in just six ODIs. In Jasprit Bumrah’s absence due to a back issue, Mohammed Shami's role becomes even more crucial in leading the pace attack in his first ODI series since the World Cup. Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma have endured a lean patch in red-ball cricket over the past few months. Whether a switch in format sparks a change in fortunes for the experienced duo is a question that will be answered over the course of this series.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks! The first leg of England's tour of India is done and dusted, with the T20I series going India's way 4-1. Now, we move on to the more consequential leg of the tour. With the Champions Trophy less than a fortnight away, this three-match series presents a crucial opportunity for both sides to round off their preparations. We kick things off here in Nagpur with the first ODI!

The countdown to cricket's elite showdown has begun! With the 2025 ICC Champions Trophy just around the corner, the spotlight shifts to a riveting three-match ODI series that's more than just another tour. Nagpur, Cuttack, and Ahmedabad set the stage for what promises to be a thrilling dress rehearsal – each match a stepping stone towards cricket's coveted prize. Fresh off a dominant T20I display, Team India now regroups with added firepower as the ODI heavyweights return to the fold. The big guns are back! Rohit Sharma reclaims the captain's mantle, while run-machine Virat Kohli returns to bolster the lineup. Despite their lean run in the recent Border-Gavaskar Trophy, Rohit and Virat return to their comfort zone, the 50-over format where they've been nothing short of phenomenal. The batting order packs a punch, with highly talented Shubman Gill fighting for the spot in the top with Yashasvi Jaiswal, while the middle-order fortress stands strong with Shreyas Iyer and Hardik Pandya. Behind the stumps, a strategic battle brews between KL Rahul's technical prowess and Rishabh Pant's left-handed dynamite. In the spin department, Jadeja leads a potent trio, with Axar and Washington providing rich alternatives. The mystery men are back too. Kuldeep Yadav returns after his October layoff, while Varun Chakravarthy rides his recent wave of success. With Jasprit Bumrah available only for the Ahmedabad showdown, pace duties fall to the ever-reliable Mohammed Shami and Arshdeep Singh, with rookie Harshit Rana waiting in the wings. England's ODI fortunes need a desperate revival! Once kings of white-ball cricket, the Three Lions now find themselves surprisingly languishing at seventh in the ICC rankings, a position that hardly befits their pedigree. Their run in this format hasn’t been promising since their dismal World Cup 2023 campaign. They have faced consecutive series defeats against West Indies and Australia. Enter Jos Jos Buttler's brigade, armed with a point to prove and talent to spare. The batting lineup sees the classic touch of Joe Root at his sweet spot of number three, while the explosive duo of Ben Duckett and Phil Salt gear up to set the Powerplay ablaze. The middle-order puzzle presents an intriguing choice between newcomers Jacob Bethell and Jamie Smith, flanked by the proven firepower of Harry Brook and Liam Livingstone. Fresh from their T20I heroics, all-round sensations Brydon Carse and Jamie Overton add depth to both departments. The pace arsenal remains intimidatingly fiery with Jofra Archer, Mark Wood, Saqib Mahmood, and Gus Atkinson forming a quartet that can rattle any batting lineup on their day. And the mystery man, Adil Rashid remains as the spin chief of the squad. After a six-year hiatus, Nagpur's Vidarbha Cricket Association Stadium is set to host One Day International cricket once again. For Team India, this marks their first ODI on home turf since the 2023 World Cup, as they look to redeem themselves following their disappointing loss to Sri Lanka last year in an away series. Their track record at home though has been quite stellar, with just one series defeat at home in the last 5 years. As for England, their last ODI series win against India in India came back in 1984, with the second-best performance being carrying out a draw in 2001/02, hence it has been a long wait for the tourists. Will England challenge the Men in Blue this time around? A cracker of a series awaits!
